skill.name: competitor-teardown
skill.description: Guides structured competitor teardown work using feature matrices, pricing comparisons, SWOT analysis, positioning maps, review mining, and UX screenshot workflows.
skill.summary: Create structured competitor teardown reports for product strategy and market research.
skill.author: halt-catch-fire

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally uses belt, npx, browser automation, search services, and a hosted Python executor. Most static backtick findings were Markdown false positives, but the actual command blocks and external URLs are confirmed as medium and low risk capabilities.

remediation.issue: External command execution is central to the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running belt or npx commands, especially installs and commands that send URLs to third-party services.

remediation.issue: Hosted Python execution is presented as a normal report generation step.
remediation.suggestion: Document that Python executor input should be reviewed before execution and should not include secrets, credentials, or private datasets.

remediation.issue: Research targets and screenshots are sent to external services.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users not to submit confidential competitor lists, internal strategy notes, or private customer data to third-party research apps.

content.value_statement: Competitive research often becomes scattered across screenshots, notes, and pricing pages. This skill provides a repeatable teardown framework for strategy-ready reports.
actual_capabilities: Defines a seven-layer competitor analysis framework covering product, pricing, positioning, traction, reviews, content, and team signals.
Provides command examples for web search, page extraction, screenshots, review mining, and image stitching through belt apps.
Includes templates for feature matrices, pricing comparisons, SWOT tables, positioning maps, and executive summaries.
Shows how to generate a positioning map with Python and save it as an image artifact.
Lists review sources and extraction prompts for G2, Capterra, app stores, Product Hunt, and Reddit.
limitations: Requires the belt CLI and access to external inference.sh applications for command examples.
Does not verify data accuracy without current research and source review.
Uses placeholder competitor names and URLs that users must replace.
Does not automate legal review for scraping, screenshots, or terms of service limits.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Teardown
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze three direct competitors in [market]. Focus on product, pricing, positioning, and user reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Feature Matrix
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a feature matrix comparing [our product] with [competitors]. Include availability, plan limits, and source notes for each feature.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Pricing and Packaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare pricing pages for [competitors]. Summarize tiers, limits, annual discounts, hidden costs, and implications for our packaging.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an Executive Teardown
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an executive competitor teardown for [market]. Include SWOT, positioning map, review themes, screenshots to collect, and strategic recommendations.

output_examples.input: Compare three project management competitors for a product planning meeting.
output_examples.output: A report outline with market summary, feature matrix, pricing table, review themes, positioning map, and recommended opportunities.

output_examples.input: Review a competitor pricing page and summarize risks for our packaging.
Mine reviews for why customers switch away from a competitor.
output_examples.output: A review analysis grouped by complaints, praised features, switching triggers, missing features, and sales messaging opportunities.

best_practices: Date every source and refresh research before major decisions.
Compare only the top direct competitors unless the goal requires a broad landscape.
Separate observed facts from strategic interpretation in every deliverable.
anti_patterns: Do not treat competitor marketing copy as verified product capability.
Do not publish screenshots or scraped data without checking source permissions.
Do not hide competitor strengths to make your product appear better.

faq.question: Does this skill perform the research automatically?
faq.answer: It provides workflows and command examples. Actual research depends on available belt apps, access, and user-approved commands.

faq.question: Can I use it without the belt CLI?
faq.answer: Yes, but the command examples become manual research steps. The frameworks and templates still apply.

faq.question: What competitors should I include?
faq.answer: Start with three to five direct competitors. Add indirect competitors only when they affect positioning or buying decisions.

faq.question: How current should the data be?
faq.answer: Use the latest available public sources. Refresh pricing, reviews, and positioning before leadership or investor use.

faq.question: Can this create visual deliverables?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes positioning map and screenshot comparison workflows that can support presentation-ready visuals.

faq.question: What data should I avoid sharing?
faq.answer: Avoid secrets, private customer data, unreleased strategy, and confidential competitor lists when using external research services.
